title: Television: Wings on The Mike Yarwood Christmas Special | 1977
content:
Wings filmed an appearance on The Mike Yarwood Christmas Special at BBC Television Centre in London on 10 December 1977.

They were joined by the Campbeltown Pipe Band for a mimed performance of ‘Mull Of Kintyre’, which had just topped the UK singles chart. The previous day Wings had learnt that it had sold 500,000 copies, making it qualify for a gold disc.

A dress rehearsal took place in the afternoon, and recording happened in front of a studio audience. Wings mimed to a mix created on 7 December known as the ‘Master Backing Track – Full Length’ mix.

The ‘Mull Of Kintyre’ sequence was filmed at around 10pm. Paul McCartney also took part in a comedy sketch with Yarwood.

The show was broadcast at 8.20pm on Christmas Day. It was seen by 21.4 million people, making it the most-watched Christmas show in British television history.

Although ‘Mull Of Kintyre’ was already a hit, the programme helped make sales go stratospheric. As Denny Laine later recalled, “We did the Mike Yarwood show at Christmas time with it. That made it huge.”
